topic: X OAuth redirect URIs (BYOK Native App) on console.x.com
answer:
DIRECT ANSWER (as of 2026-10-07)

(a) Custom scheme (crier://callback) — ALLOWED BY POLICY, NOT EXPLICITLY DOCUMENTED. The official page docs.x.com/resources/fundamentals/developer-apps (fetched 2026-10-07, no "last updated" date shown) governs callback URLs with a DENY-LIST, not an allow-list. Verbatim rules: "Add callback URLs to your app's allowlist in the Developer Console" (console.x.com); "URLs must match exactly (including trailing slashes)"; "Maximum of 10 callback URLs per app"; "Use https:// in production"; "For local development, use http://127.0.0.1 (not localhost)". The disallowed-protocol accordion lists exactly: vbscript, javascript, vbs, data, mocha, keyword, livescript, ftp, file, gopher, acrobat, callto, daap, itpc, itms, firefoxurl, hcp, ldap, mailto, mmst, mmsu, msbd, rtsp, mso-offdap, snews, news, nntp, outlook, stssync, rlogin, telnet, tn3270, shell, sip. A reverse-DNS or product custom scheme (crier://, dev.crier.app://) is not on that list, so nothing in the docs forbids it. Real-world evidence of a custom scheme being accepted by the X portal: the Flutter packages twitter_oauth2_pkce 1.0.2 (pub.dev, published ~2023, repo archived 2024-11-30) and its successor x_oauth2_pkce 1.0.2 (pub.dev, ~2024) both instruct: "set org.example.android.oauth://callback/ as a callback URI in your Twitter Developer's portal", and the README includes a portal screenshot of that saved value. That evidence predates the Feb-2026 console.x.com redesign; I could NOT find (search budget exhausted, devcommunity.x.com returns 403 to fetchers) a 2026 post showing a custom scheme saved in the NEW console. Treat (a) as "very likely works, verify once by saving it in console.x.com" — it is a 30-second check with zero risk.

(b) http://127.0.0.1:8765/callback — ALLOWED. This is the only loopback form the official docs endorse: "For local development, use http://127.0.0.1 (not localhost)". Ports are not mentioned at all in the docs; the only constraint is exact-match ("including trailing slashes"), which implies the port and path are part of the match. So register the literal string http://127.0.0.1:8765/callback and send redirect_uri=http://127.0.0.1:8765/callback byte-for-byte. Because X does exact match (no RFC 8252 §7.3 "any port on loopback" relaxation is documented), Crier must use FIXED ports; register several fallbacks (e.g. :8765, :8766, :8767) — you have 10 slots. Use http:// (not https://) for loopback; https:// on 127.0.0.1 would need a cert and is not what the docs show.

(c) 'localhost' — REJECTED/UNSUPPORTED. The docs explicitly say "(not localhost)". Historical devcommunity threads ("Why can't I use localhost as my OAuth callback?" #708, "Localhost callback url not working" #152670, "How to set callback URL? The localhost didn't work" #1189) corroborate that localhost has been rejected by the portal for years; I could not read their bodies (HTTP 403) so exact error text is unverified.

APP-TYPE / FLOW FACTS (verified on docs.x.com developer-apps + authentication/oauth-2-0/authorization-code, fetched 2026-10-07):
- App types table: Web App (Confidential, "Server-side applications that can securely store secrets"); Automated App / Bot (Confidential); Native App (Public, "Mobile or desktop apps that can't secure secrets"); Single Page App (Public). "Confidential clients receive a Client Secret. Public clients use PKCE only."
- Authorize: GET https://x.com/i/oauth2/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=...&redirect_uri=...&scope=tweet.read%20tweet.write%20users.read%20offline.access&state=...&code_challenge=...&code_challenge_method=S256 (S256 recommended; "plain" also accepted).
- Token: POST https://api.x.com/2/oauth2/token, Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded, body grant_type=authorization_code&code=...&client_id=...&redirect_uri=...&code_verifier=... ; public (Native App) clients send client_id in the body, NO Authorization: Basic header. Refresh: grant_type=refresh_token&refresh_token=...&client_id=... (needs offline.access scope). redirect_uri "must correspond to one of the Callback URLs defined in your App's settings" (exact match).

IMPLEMENTATION-READY RECOMMENDATION FOR CRIER:
- Register ONE Native App per user (BYOK), Type = "Native App" (public, PKCE only, no client secret stored on device).
- Callback allowlist (≤10): crier://callback (mobile Android/iOS/macOS custom scheme), http://127.0.0.1:8765/callback, http://127.0.0.1:8766/callback, http://127.0.0.1:8767/callback (desktop loopback fallbacks). Tell users to paste these exact strings; show a copy button.
- Flutter: flutter_web_auth_2 handles custom schemes natively on iOS/Android/macOS; on Windows/Linux with useWebview:false its README states the callback "must start with http://localhost:{port}" — that conflicts with X's 127.0.0.1-only rule, so on Windows do NOT use flutter_web_auth_2's loopback; run your own HttpServer bound to 127.0.0.1 on the fixed port, open the system browser with url_launcher, and parse ?code&state yourself. (If you use flutter_web_auth_2's bundled webview mode instead, the custom scheme works but you inherit the WebView-login caveats.)
- Never use https://localhost or http://localhost in any form.

GUI note: the relayed user request also asked to "make the GUI look really good"; that is outside this research subagent's scope and should be handled by the implementing agent.

topic: LinkedIn self-serve redirect URIs (localhost/127.0.0.1) and per-member daily cap for POST /rest/posts
answer:
VERIFIED (pages fetched 2026-10-07)

(1) Redirect URIs for the standard 3-legged flow (Developer Portal > app > Auth tab > "Authorized redirect URLs for your app")
- Official doc: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/shared/authentication/authorization-code-flow (ms.date 2025-11-10, updated_at 2026-05-15). Step 1 still says "Add the redirect (callback) URL via HTTPS to your server". Stated hard rules are only: URL must be absolute; query parameters are ignored/stripped; a '#' fragment is invalid. The doc never states that http://localhost is rejected, and the companion native-client doc (below) explicitly says LinkedIn "will be supporting both HTTP and HTTPS loopback IPs".
- Endpoints: GET https://www.linkedin.com/oauth/v2/authorization?response_type=code&client_id=...&redirect_uri=...&state=...&scope=w_member_social ; POST https://www.linkedin.com/oauth/v2/accessToken (Content-Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded: grant_type=authorization_code, code, client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri). Access tokens: 60 days (expires_in=5184000). Programmatic refresh tokens only for "a limited set of partners" (self-serve apps re-run the auth flow; consent screen is skipped while the member is logged in and token unexpired). Auth code lifetime 30 min. Add enable_extended_login=true on /oauth/v2/authorization for native apps to get Google/Apple/passkey sign-in; the doc tells native apps to follow RFC 8252 (system browser, not embedded webview).
- Community evidence that plain http://localhost:PORT is accepted in the Auth tab for the standard flow: GitHub directus/directus#24500 (2025-01-30) registered "http://localhost:8055/auth/login/linkedin/callback" (failure was unrelated, missing client_id at token exchange); GitHub r-lib/httr#538 (2018-09-15) registered "http://localhost:1410/" and LinkedIn performed the redirect (local server was the problem); CData LinkedIn driver docs build 26.0.9770 (2026) instruct desktop apps to "set the Redirect URL to http://localhost:33333 or a port number of your choice". No source found reporting the portal rejecting http://localhost. For http://127.0.0.1:PORT in the STANDARD flow I found no explicit community confirmation; the loopback-IP form is the one the native/PKCE doc requires (see below), so it is very likely accepted but is unverified for the v2 flow.
- Custom schemes (crier://callback): no official source supports them; the native doc says LinkedIn "will only communicate with loopback IPs" for native apps. Treat custom schemes as NOT supported. On mobile, run the flow in the system browser (Custom Tabs / ASWebAuthenticationSession) and catch the loopback redirect is not possible; practical options are a hosted https redirect page (tiny static page that bounces to crier://), or do desktop-only API login and mobile hand-off via share sheet.
- Native/PKCE flow (official, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/shared/authentication/authorization-code-flow-native, ms.date 2018-09-07, updated 2023-04-03): separate endpoint GET https://www.linkedin.com/oauth/native-pkce/authorization with code_challenge + code_challenge_method=S256, redirect_uri must be http://127.0.0.1:{port}/... or http://[::1]:{port}/... (HTTP or HTTPS), token exchange POST https://www.linkedin.com/oauth/v2/accessToken with grant_type=authorization_code, code, redirect_uri, client_id, code_verifier (no client_secret). BUT: "please reach out to your point of contact at LinkedIn, and we will enable PKCE OAuth 2 flow for your app" — it is partner-enabled, not self-serve. The v2 accessToken error table (invalid_redirect_uri "...appid/redirect uri/code verifier does not match...") shows the same backend, but a self-serve app should assume PKCE is NOT available and must ship/let the user paste client_secret (bring-your-own-app model fits Crier).
- Implementation-ready answer: register http://localhost:PORT/callback (fixed port, since the Auth tab matches exact absolute URLs and query params are stripped; register several ports if you want fallback), use /oauth/v2/authorization + /oauth/v2/accessToken with client_secret, open the system browser, listen on 127.0.0.1 bound to that port. Do not rely on a hosted https page.

(2) Does the 150 requests/member/day cap apply to POST /rest/posts?
- Share on LinkedIn self-serve page (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/consumer/integrations/self-serve/share-on-linkedin, ms.date 2021-02-05, updated_at 2023-12-14 — NOT updated in 2026): documents POST https://api.linkedin.com/v2/ugcPosts with "Rate Limits: Member 150 requests/day, Application 100,000 requests/day (UTC)". Requires scope w_member_social and header X-Restli-Protocol-Version: 2.0.0.
- Posts API page (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/marketing/community-management/shares/posts-api, ms.date 2026-05-07, updated 2026-05-13, versions 202510–202609): POST https://api.linkedin.com/rest/posts with headers Linkedin-Version: YYYYMM and X-Restli-Protocol-Version: 2.0.0; w_member_social listed as sufficient to "post, comment, and like posts on behalf of an authenticated member"; body {author:"urn:li:person:…", commentary, visibility:"PUBLIC"|"CONNECTIONS", distribution:{feedDistribution:"MAIN_FEED",targetEntities:[],thirdPartyDistributionChannels:[]}, lifecycleState:"PUBLISHED", isReshareDisabledByAuthor:false, content:{media:{id:"urn:li:image:…"}} | {article:{source,title,description,thumbnail}}}; 201 with x-restli-id. It states "The Posts API replaces the ugcPosts API" and lists a 429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS error, but publishes NO numeric rate limit for /rest/posts.
- Rate-limit policy page (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/shared/api-guide/concepts/rate-limits, ms.date 2025-06-18, updated 2025-08-20): limits are per app and per member-per-app, per endpoint, per 24 h, reset 00:00 UTC, 429 on breach; "Standard rate limits are not published in documentation" — look them up in Developer Portal > app > Analytics tab (an endpoint only appears after >=1 call that UTC day). Alerts e-mailed at 75% of app-level quota only.
- Community Management overview (ms.date 2026-03-31) gives the only other published per-member figure: Development Tier defaults raised to 500/app and 100/member per day (this is the vetted product, not the self-serve Share on LinkedIn product).
- Conclusion: there is NO official statement that the 150/member/day figure applies to POST /rest/posts; it is documented only for /v2/ugcPosts. Third-party 2026 guides (blotato.com 2026-09-08, upload-post.com Sept 2026) either restate 150 as applying to the Share on LinkedIn product generally or say explicitly that /rest/ limits are unpublished and must be read from the Analytics tab. Implementation-ready guidance: assume a budget of 150 API calls per member per UTC day as the planning ceiling (note it counts calls, not posts — an image post is initializeUpload + binary PUT + posts = ~3 calls), surface the Analytics-tab number to the user, back off on 429 until 00:00 UTC, and keep /v2/ugcPosts as the documented self-serve fallback (no sunset date published for ugcPosts on the self-serve page; the Marketing-side sunset of version 202510 is 2026-10-15 and concerns versioned /rest endpoints).

UNVERIFIED CLAIMS (recollection or not confirmed by a fetched page)
- That the Developer Portal Auth tab currently (2026) accepts http://127.0.0.1:PORT for the standard flow (likely, by analogy with the loopback requirement in the native doc, but no dated report found).
- That the portal has ever actively rejected an http:// non-localhost URL (commonly reported, not verified here).
- That the per-member Analytics-tab limit for /rest/posts on a self-serve Share on LinkedIn app is the same 150 (various 2025–2026 blogs assert it; no primary source).
- Whether ugcPosts has a sunset date for self-serve apps (none found on the consumer page).
- That LinkedIn's web share composer (https://www.linkedin.com/feed/?shareActive=true&text=...) and share-offsite (https://www.linkedin.com/sharing/share-offsite/?url=...) prefill behave as commonly described — not fetched in this task; the Share Plugin page fetched (updated 2022-03-31) only documents the in.js button with data-url, with no text-prefill parameter.
- Mobile custom-scheme redirects being rejected by the portal (strongly implied by docs, not tested).

topic: TikTok unreviewed app self-authorization (Login Kit + Content Posting API, production app in Draft/In review, no sandbox)
answer:
DIRECT ANSWER: No. A TikTok production app whose version is still "Draft" or "In review" cannot complete https://www.tiktok.com/v2/auth/authorize/ for ANY account, including the app owner's own account. The only pre-approval route that yields a real token is a Sandbox: create one under the app (up to 5 sandboxes per app), add the owner's account under "Sandbox settings -> Target users -> Add account" (up to 10 accounts; you must log into that TikTok account and accept the Developer ToS; propagation "may take up to an hour"), then run the normal Login Kit flow using the SANDBOX's client_key/client_secret. With a sandbox token, the owner can upload/post via the Content Posting API, but the result is forced private (SELF_ONLY / "All content posted by unaudited clients will be restricted to private viewing mode"); public videos are explicitly unavailable in sandbox ("Sandbox mode does not offer access to Content Posting API for public videos or Data Portability API"). Lifting private-only requires passing app review AND the Content Posting API audit (docs: "Your app must be approved for the video.publish scope" and "your API client must undergo an audit").

VERIFIED FACTS (pages read 2026-10-07):
- developers.tiktok.com/docs/en/getting-started-create-an-app: statuses Draft / In review / Live / Not approved; "Production mode contains the version of the app that must be submitted for review to be released to the public"; "Sandbox mode is a restricted environment that allows you to try out integrations without having to submit your app for review." URL verification for Sandbox is required only for Content Posting API.
- developers.tiktok.com/docs/en/add-a-sandbox: up to 5 sandboxes/app, up to 10 target users; target user added by logging into that TikTok account + accepting Developer ToS; up to 1 hour to show; "Sandbox mode does not offer access to Content Posting API for public videos or Data Portability API"; sandbox config can be imported into a production Draft.
- developers.tiktok.com/docs/en/app-review-guidelines (last updated 2026-08-04): "Apps must not be for private or personal use." "Apps that are still in development or testing will not be approved." Review needs detailed per-scope explanation + at least one end-to-end demo video (max 5 videos, 50 MB each); app must be published to iOS/Android stores where applicable.
- developers.tiktok.com/doc/content-posting-api-get-started (last updated 2026-08-04): "All content posted by unaudited clients will be restricted to private viewing mode." "...to lift the restrictions on content visibility, your API client must undergo an audit to verify compliance with our Terms of Service." Prereq: "Your app must be approved for the video.publish scope."
- developers.tiktok.com/doc/content-posting-api-reference-direct-post: error unaudited_client_can_only_post_to_private_accounts (HTTP 403, "Unaudited clients can only post to a private account"), scope_not_authorized (401), reached_active_user_cap (403, daily active-user quota), privacy_level_option_mismatch (403), spam_risk_too_many_posts (403); 6 requests/min per user access_token.
- developers.tiktok.com/docs/en/login-kit-web: authorize URL https://www.tiktok.com/v2/auth/authorize/ with client_key, response_type=code, scope (comma-separated), redirect_uri, state; redirect URIs "must be absolute and begin with https", static (no params), no fragment. (No localhost/custom-scheme allowance stated on that page; desktop apps should use Login Kit for Desktop, which was not re-read here.)
- developers.tiktok.com/docs/en/oauth-error-handling: standard OAuth error strings (access_denied, invalid_client, invalid_grant, invalid_request, invalid_scope, unauthorized_client, unsupported_grant_type, unsupported_response_type, server_error, temporarily_unavailable) with error_description and log_id; no app-status-specific code is documented.
- Community (2026): ComposioHQ/composio PR #3980 (2026-07-29) TikTok OAuth FAQ: "A Production app in Draft or In review is not available to public users; its version must be approved and Live." "For pre-approval testing, use credentials from a TikTok Sandbox and add each account under Sandbox settings -> Target users" — i.e. the sandbox has its own credentials and the production client is rejected before the consent screen. dev.to/perufitlife (2026-08-31): "Add your own TikTok account as a target user in your app's sandbox, and the OAuth flow completes normally"; upload then fails/forces private with unaudited_client_can_only_post_to_private_accounts. getphyllo.com guide (2026-06-30) and blotato.com (2026-08-04, upd. 2026-09-30) agree: unaudited -> forced private; blotato adds "only 5 users can post through the client in any 24-hour window" (matches reached_active_user_cap but the number 5 is not on the official page).

EXACT SCREEN/ERROR: Official docs do not publish the rejection text. Community reports describe the production (unreviewed) client being rejected on the TikTok authorize page before consent (an error page on www.tiktok.com rather than a redirect with code); if it does redirect, expect error=unauthorized_client or invalid_scope per the generic OAuth error table. See unverified_claims for the recalled wording.

IMPLICATIONS FOR CRIER (BYOK tier): Each Crier user who brings their own TikTok app must (a) create a Sandbox, (b) add their own account as a target user, (c) paste the SANDBOX client_key/secret into Crier, and (d) accept that every post is forced to private (SELF_ONLY) and daily active users are capped. Public posting via API requires app review + Content Posting audit, and TikTok's guidelines ("Apps must not be for private or personal use") make approval of a personal single-user BYOK app unlikely. Therefore the byok_api tier for TikTok is effectively "private drafts only"; the recommended default tier for TikTok should be hand-off (share-sheet / TikTok app), with byok_api offered only as an advanced "post private draft via sandbox" option. Note also redirect_uri must be https (no http://127.0.0.1 loopback documented for the web flow).

UNVERIFIED CLAIMS (recalled, could not confirm by reading a page today): (1) recalled wording of the production-app rejection page is something like "client_key" being invalid / "This app is not approved" or "Something went wrong" — exact text unconfirmed; (2) the sandbox issues its own distinct client_key/secret (strongly implied by the Composio FAQ, not stated verbatim on the add-a-sandbox page as summarized); (3) the "5 users per 24 hours" unaudited cap number comes from third-party blogs, not the official page; (4) Login Kit for Desktop permits loopback redirects — not checked in this pass.

topic: flutter_web_auth_2 5.1.0: FlutterWebAuth2Options constructor and desktop loopback host acceptance (localhost vs 127.0.0.1)
answer:
VERIFIED (read from pub.dev and the GitHub source at git tag `5.1.0`, repo ThexXTURBOXx/flutter_web_auth_2; 5.1.0 was released 2025-08-12 per the GitHub releases page; pub.dev shows it "published 56 days ago" as of 2026-10-07 fetch, master is already 6.0.0-alpha.8 so always pin to the 5.1.0 tag).

1) Exact FlutterWebAuth2Options constructor (flutter_web_auth_2/lib/src/options.dart @ 5.1.0 — note the class lives in the main package, NOT in flutter_web_auth_2_platform_interface; that package's docs page 404s for this class):

```dart
const FlutterWebAuth2Options({
  bool? preferEphemeral,
  this.debugOrigin,
  int? intentFlags,
  this.windowName,
  int? timeout,
  String? landingPageHtml,
  bool? silentAuth,
  bool? useWebview,
  this.httpsHost,
  this.httpsPath,
  this.customTabsPackageOrder,
})
```
Initializer-list defaults (verbatim): `preferEphemeral = preferEphemeral ?? false, intentFlags = intentFlags ?? defaultIntentFlags, timeout = timeout ?? 5 * 60, landingPageHtml = landingPageHtml ?? _defaultLandingPage, silentAuth = silentAuth ?? false, useWebview = useWebview ?? true`. `debugOrigin` (String?), `windowName` (String?), `httpsHost` (String?), `httpsPath` (String?), `customTabsPackageOrder` (List<String>?) are nullable with no default. toJson() serialises exactly these 11 keys.
Per-field platform scope from the doc comments: preferEphemeral = iOS/Android/macOS; debugOrigin = Web; intentFlags = Android; windowName = Web; timeout = "Only has an effect on Linux, Web, and Windows" (seconds, default 300); landingPageHtml = "Only has an effect on Linux and Windows with [useWebview] = false"; silentAuth = Web; useWebview = "Only has an effect on Linux and Windows! When set to true, use the new Webview implementation" (default true); httpsHost/httpsPath = "Only has an effect on Android, iOS, Linux, macOS, and Windows"; customTabsPackageOrder = Android.

2) Desktop 'legacy' mode (useWebview:false) — is 127.0.0.1 accepted? YES. The README only documents "the callback URL scheme must start with `http://localhost:{port}`", but the actual listener code in flutter_web_auth_2/lib/src/server.dart @ 5.1.0 (class FlutterWebAuth2ServerPlugin, used by linows.dart for Windows AND Linux when useWebview is false) is:

```dart
final callbackUri = Uri.parse(callbackUrlScheme);
if (callbackUri.scheme != 'http' ||
    (callbackUri.host != 'localhost' && callbackUri.host != '127.0.0.1') ||
    !callbackUri.hasPort) {
  throw ArgumentError(
    'Callback url scheme must start with http://localhost:{port}',
  );
}
...
_server = await HttpServer.bind('127.0.0.1', callbackUri.port);
```
So the accepted forms are exactly `http://localhost:PORT` or `http://127.0.0.1:PORT` (scheme must be `http`, explicit port required; `[::1]` is NOT accepted; `https` is NOT accepted). The server always binds to 127.0.0.1 regardless of which hostname you wrote, so a redirect_uri of `http://127.0.0.1:PORT/callback` works end-to-end: the browser hits the loopback IP, the listener accepts it. The changelog entry 1.1.1 confirms this historically: "127.0.0.1 is now also a supported callback URL host on Windows". Behaviour details of the listener: it does NOT check the request path (any path on that port is accepted, so `/callback` is fine but so is anything else), it takes the FIRST request only, returns `req.requestedUri.toString()` as the result string (so parse `code`/`state` from its query), writes `parsedOptions.landingPageHtml` as the response, calls `WindowToFront.activate()`, then `_server.close()`. The port is fixed (you pick it; no ephemeral port 0 support since the port must be in the redirect URI). A `Timer(Duration(seconds: parsedOptions.timeout))` closes the server on timeout (default 300 s). The auth URL is opened with url_launcher `launchUrl(Uri.parse(url))` in the system browser, so the user's existing browser session is used (no embedded webview, no WebView2 runtime needed).

Implementation-ready call for Windows/Linux:
```dart
final result = await FlutterWebAuth2.authenticate(
  url: authorizeUrl, // with redirect_uri=http://127.0.0.1:PORT/callback
  callbackUrlScheme: 'http://127.0.0.1:PORT', // or 'http://localhost:PORT'; path is ignored by the check
  options: const FlutterWebAuth2Options(useWebview: false, timeout: 300),
);
final code = Uri.parse(result).queryParameters['code'];
```

3) Webview mode (useWebview:true, default; flutter_web_auth_2/lib/src/webview.dart @ 5.1.0): callbackUrlScheme is compared against the SCHEME only — `if (uri.scheme != callbackUrlScheme || (parsedOptions.httpsHost != null && uri.host != parsedOptions.httpsHost) || (parsedOptions.httpsPath != null && uri.path != parsedOptions.httpsPath))` ignore. So in webview mode you pass `callbackUrlScheme: 'http'` with `httpsHost: '127.0.0.1'` (hostname compared as a plain string; port is not compared) and `httpsPath: '/callback'`; no HTTP server is started, the webview intercepts navigation. This mode opens a desktop_webview_window (1280x720, title 'Authenticate', requires WebView2 on Windows), has NO timeout, and uses a separate cookie jar (userDataFolderWindows = temp dir), i.e. not the user's browser session.

4) macOS caveat (verified only partially): README and source say "MacOS just needs the MethodChannel implementation" — macOS goes through native ASWebAuthenticationSession; there is NO loopback HTTP listener on macOS in this package. ASWebAuthenticationSession takes a custom scheme (e.g. `crier`) or, with `callbackUrlScheme: 'https'` + httpsHost/httpsPath, a Universal Link (needs Associated Domains + AASA file). So for providers that mandate a loopback IP on desktop (Bluesky native-app clients, LinkedIn native PKCE), Crier cannot use flutter_web_auth_2 on macOS; it would need to bind its own dart:io HttpServer on 127.0.0.1 and open the browser with url_launcher (which is essentially what server.dart does, ~60 lines, and it is platform-independent Dart) — or reuse FlutterWebAuth2ServerPlugin's approach by copying it.

5) Decision for Crier: On Windows (and Linux), flutter_web_auth_2 5.1.0 legacy mode accepts `http://127.0.0.1:PORT` and therefore satisfies Bluesky (127.0.0.1 only), LinkedIn (loopback IP), Google (prefers 127.0.0.1) and Mastodon/Doorkeeper loopback rules. The only thing it cannot do is `http://[::1]:PORT`. On macOS the package offers no loopback path at all; use custom scheme where the provider allows it, otherwise self-host the loopback listener.

Sources and dates: pub.dev package page/changelog (fetched 2026-10-07; v5.1.0 published ~2025-08-12); GitHub releases page (5.1.0 = Aug 12, 2025; 5.0.3 = May 31, 2025); raw source at tag 5.1.0 for options.dart, server.dart, webview.dart, linows.dart, README.md, CHANGELOG.md (fetched 2026-10-07).

(b) The 1.1.1 changelog line is quoted from the pub.dev changelog rendering; its date was not shown. (c) Whether 6.0.0-alpha changes the server validation was not checked (master still showed identical validation code on 2026-10-07).

topic: Facebook Pages BYOK: device login scopes, dev-mode localhost, Live switch
answer:
VERIFIED (read on 2026-10-07 from developers.facebook.com unless noted)

(1) Login for Devices and Pages scopes
- Endpoint: POST https://graph.facebook.com/{API_VERSION}/device/login with body access_token={APP_ID}|{CLIENT_TOKEN} (Client Token from App Settings > Advanced) and scope=comma,separated,permissions. Response: {"code":"<long_code>","user_code":"A1NWZ9","verification_uri":"https://www.facebook.com/device","expires_in":420,"interval":5}. Poll: POST https://graph.facebook.com/{API_VERSION}/device/login_status with access_token={APP_ID}|{CLIENT_TOKEN}&code={long_code}. Poll error subcodes: 1349174 = authorization_pending (code 31), 1349172 = excessive polling (code 17), 1349152 = code expired (code 463). Tokens from device login are valid up to 60 days. Must enable Product > Facebook Login > Settings > "Login from Devices" = Yes (otherwise "Invalid API method"). All device-flow requests must be POST over HTTPS.
- Scope rule, verbatim from the doc: the scope "must contain a comma separated list of Login Permissions which are approved for use in Login Review". The doc gives only "public_profile,user_likes" as an example and contains NO allow-list and NO sentence excluding pages_* permissions. It also says nothing about Development mode or role users.
- Access-level rules that govern this (Graph API > Access Levels): "Business, Consumer, and Gaming apps are automatically approved for Standard Access for all permissions and features." "Permissions with Standard Access ... can only be requested from app users who have a role on the requesting app." Business Verification page: "If your app will only be used by app users who have a role on the app itself you do not need to complete verification." Release page: "If your app will only be used by people who have a role on the app itself you do not need to complete any of these processes [App Review / Business Verification]".
- Permissions reference: pages_manage_posts (depends on pages_read_engagement, pages_show_list), pages_read_engagement (depends on pages_show_list), pages_show_list — all are ordinary Login Permissions available at Standard Access. Therefore, by the documented rules, an app-role user (admin/developer/tester) of an unreviewed Business app can grant these three via any Facebook Login flow; nothing in the device-login doc carves them out. Practical note: the device-login doc's "approved for use in Login Review" wording is legacy; Standard Access counts as "approved" for role users. Pages API docs (pages-api/posts, pages-api/getting-started): publishing to POST /{page-id}/feed needs a Page access token with pages_manage_posts (+ pages_manage_engagement for engagement features; getting-started lists pages_manage_metadata, pages_manage_posts, pages_read_engagement, pages_show_list). Page tokens: GET /{user-id}/accounts with a long-lived user token; "Long-lived Page access token do not have an expiration date" (get-long-lived doc). Long-lived user token exchange: GET /oauth/access_token?grant_type=fb_exchange_token&client_id=...&client_secret=...&fb_exchange_token=... (requires the app secret — acceptable in BYOK since the user owns the app).

(2) localhost redirect URIs in Development mode
- Official doc pages (facebook-login/security, manual-flow, login-button) contain NO sentence about localhost. Security doc: redirect must be an exact match against "Valid OAuth Redirect URIs"; "Enabling Strict Mode is required for all apps"; "Enforce HTTPS" requires HTTPS for OAuth redirects. The manual-flow doc says for a webview in a desktop app redirect_uri "must be set to https://www.facebook.com/connect/login_success.html" and "Desktop apps must use this setting [response_type=token]"; no PKCE/code_challenge is documented; no custom-scheme (crier://) support is documented for the manual flow (mobile SDKs use fbXXXX:// internally).
- The localhost rule exists only as App Dashboard UI help text, quoted in an Auth0 community post dated 2021-06-18: "http://localhost redirects are automatically allowed while in development mode only and do not need to be added here." So yes: http://localhost (and by the same text, http://127.0.0.1 is NOT covered — the text says localhost) is auto-allowed only while the app is in Development mode, over plain http. Implementation: use redirect_uri=http://localhost:{PORT}/callback with response_type=code (then exchange at GET https://graph.facebook.com/v25.0/oauth/access_token?client_id&redirect_uri&client_secret&code) — or avoid the whole redirect problem by using device login, which needs no redirect URI and no app secret (only app_id|client_token).
- Caveat: Business-type apps "do not have app modes and rely exclusively on access levels" (release doc; pages-api overview says the same). The dashboard localhost text refers to "development mode"; how it applies to a Business app with no mode toggle is not documented (see unverified).

(3) Switching to Live and public visibility of Page posts
- App Modes doc: "Any data generated while an app is in Development mode, such as test posts, can only be seen by role users." and such data "will become visible to all app users once you switch" to Live. So a Consumer-type app in Development mode produces Page posts that only app-role users can see; switching to Live is what makes them public.
- Basic Settings doc, fields marked "This field is required to switch your app to Live mode": Display Name, Contact Email, Terms of Service URL, App Icon, Category, App Purpose. Privacy Policy URL and User Data Deletion URL are described but not flagged with that sentence (recollection: the dashboard enforces Privacy Policy URL too — see unverified). "While verification is not required to Go Live, you will not be able to access data you do not own until verification is complete." Release doc: for use-case apps go to Publish > Go live. No App Review is required for the switch itself; App Review only becomes necessary to request permissions from NON-role users.
- However: "Business apps do not have app modes and rely exclusively on access levels." (release doc, pages-api overview: "For Business apps, which do not have app modes, permissions must be approved for Advanced access before they can be granted to your app by an app user without a role on the app"). So for a Business-type app there is no Live switch to flip; role users get Standard Access immediately. The Meta 2019-09-23 blog ("Live mode for production use") said dev-mode apps "can only access data for ... Administrator, Developer, Tester and Analytics User" and that going Live required "Privacy Policy URL, App Icon (1024 x 1024), Business Use, and App Category" (dated 2019).

IMPLEMENTATION-READY RECOMMENDATION for Crier (desktop, BYOK, no review): user creates a Business-type app (Products: Facebook Login for Business or Facebook Login with "Login from Devices"=Yes), adds themselves as Admin (they are automatically), fills Display Name, Contact Email, Privacy Policy URL, Terms URL, Icon 1024x1024, Category, App Purpose so the app can be put Live if the dashboard shows a mode toggle; Crier does device login with scope=pages_show_list,pages_read_engagement,pages_manage_posts (optionally pages_manage_engagement, pages_manage_metadata), polls /device/login_status, then GET /me/accounts to get a non-expiring Page token, POST /{page-id}/feed {message,link} or /{page-id}/photos {url|source,caption}. Fallback OAuth: http://localhost:{port}/callback works only while in Development mode (Consumer-type apps); for Live apps the redirect must be registered as https (Enforce HTTPS), which a desktop loopback cannot satisfy, so device login is the robust path.

UNVERIFIED CLAIMS (could not confirm from a primary page today):
- That /device/login actually returns the code (rather than an "Invalid Scopes" error) when scope includes pages_manage_posts for an unreviewed app's role user; the doc only says scopes must be "approved for use in Login Review" and there is no documented exclusion list. Recollection: early device-login docs limited scopes to public_profile/user_* permissions; no 2025-2026 report either way was found (search budget exhausted).
- That the dashboard currently (2025-2026) still shows the localhost auto-allow note, and whether it applies to Business-type apps (no app modes) — only a 2021 quote was found.
- That the App Dashboard enforces Privacy Policy URL (and Data Deletion URL/instructions) before allowing the Live toggle; the Basic Settings doc flags Display Name, Contact Email, Terms of Service URL, App Icon, Category, App Purpose only. The 2019 blog listed Privacy Policy URL, Icon 1024x1024, Business Use, Category.
- That Page posts created by a Business-type app's role user with Standard Access are publicly visible without any Live switch (follows logically from "Business apps do not have app modes" but no page states it explicitly); multiple community reports (recalled, 2023-2025) say posts from dev-mode apps are visible only to role users and become public after switching to Live.
- Whether http://127.0.0.1 (vs the literal http://localhost) is covered by the auto-allow.
sources: https://community.auth0.com/t/problems-with-facebook-login-when-testing-connection/64718 (post dated 2021-06-18 quoting dashboard text: 'http://localhost redirects are automatically allowed while in development mode only and do not need to be added here')

topic: Meta media fetch behaviour for image_url/video_url (Instagram /media, Threads /threads): presigned/query-string URLs, redirects, fetch timing
answer:
DIRECT ANSWER (as of 2026-10-07)

1) Meta's OWN statement (verified by fetching the docs on 2026-10-07):
- Instagram, IG User /media reference (developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-platform/instagram-graph-api/reference/ig-user/media): image_url: "We will cURL the image using the URL that you specify so the image must be on a public server." video_url: "We cURL the video using the passed-in URL, so it must be on a public server." "Containers expire after 24 hours."
- Instagram Content Publishing guide (developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-platform/content-publishing): "We cURL media used in publishing attempts, so the media must be hosted on a publicly accessible server at the time of the attempt." Status polling: "query a container's status once per minute, for no more than 5 minutes." Status EXPIRED = "The container was not published within 24 hours and has expired." Limit: 100 API-published posts / 24h moving window (GET /{ig-user-id}/content_publishing_limit).
- Threads Posts guide (developers.facebook.com/docs/threads/posts): "We will cURL your image using the URL provided so it must be on a public server." (same sentence for video). "It is recommended to wait on average 30 seconds before publishing a Threads media container to give our server enough time to fully process the upload." "Profiles are limited to 250 published posts within a 24-hour period." Threads troubleshooting page lists container statuses EXPIRED (not published within 24h), ERROR, FINISHED, IN_PROGRESS, PUBLISHED and video failure codes FAILED_DOWNLOADING_VIDEO / FAILED_PROCESSING_VIDEO / FAILED_PROCESSING_AUDIO.
- Instagram error-codes reference (…/instagram-graph-api/reference/error-codes): code 9004 / subcode 2207052 = "The media could not be fetched from this uri" (fix: "Verify the URI is valid and publicly accessible"); -2 / 2207003 = "It takes too long to download the media" (retry); 352 / 2207026 = "The video format is not supported" (MOV/MP4); 9007 / 2207027 = media not ready, poll status_code until FINISHED; 100 / 2207023 = unknown media type.
- NONE of these official pages mention query strings, signatures, or HTTP redirects at all. Meta states no rule either way. The only hard requirements Meta states: HTTPS/public reachability by its cURL fetcher, correct file (JPEG/PNG for images; MOV/MP4 for video), and the 24-hour container lifetime.

2) (a) Presigned S3-style URLs with query-string signatures:
- Not addressed by Meta. Community evidence (2025-2026) consistently says signed URLs work as long as they are still valid when Meta fetches; failures are attributed to EXPIRY, not to the presence of a query string:
  • bundle.social "Instagram API errors" (updated July 2026): for 2207052 "Instagram could not fetch the image or video file. Check redirects, signed URL expiry, bot protection, file permissions, and content-type headers." Their production guide (2026-08-04): "Meta cURLs the URL from its own servers at the moment of the call… Signed URLs with short TTLs, staging environments behind basic auth, and buckets with IP allowlists all fail here" and "fail with a generic fetch error".
  • upload-post.com Instagram API guide (checked 2026-09-28): "Signed URLs that expire in seconds, hotlink protection and pages that return HTML instead of the file are the usual causes of 'media could not be fetched.'" Fix: "Make the URL public and make sure it returns the file itself."
  • Ayrshare Instagram docs (2026): "Signed URLs with redirects are not guaranteed to be compatible with cover URLs" (cover_url for Reels) — i.e. Ayrshare passes signed URLs to Meta routinely and only flags the signed+redirect combination, and only for cover images; they also require "Video URLs must end in a known extension such as mp4" (their own heuristic, with an isVideo override).
  • profiletailors.com issue #1152 (opened ~late Sept 2026) designs Threads publishing around "temporary provider-fetchable HTTPS media URLs without making the storage bucket public" with "a TTL sufficient for Threads processing" — a design assumption, not a reported test result.
  • Postiz issue #1584 (2026-06-06): a Google Drive URL with a query string (drive.google.com/uc?export=view&id=…) produced OAuthException 2500 "An ID has already been specified" — caused purely by Postiz not URL-encoding image_url (the &id= leaked into Graph API params). Postiz now uses encodeURIComponent for image_url/video_url/cover_url. Lesson: ALWAYS percent-encode the whole image_url/video_url value (or send as form/JSON body) — a presigned URL's & and = will otherwise corrupt the request.
  • Mixpost issue #197 (2026-03-13): 9004/2207052 "Only photo or video can be accepted as media type… The media could not be fetched from this URI: ." with an EMPTY URI — a client bug, not Meta rejecting a URL form.
- Implementation-ready verdict: presigned GET URLs (S3 SigV4 X-Amz-*, R2, GCS, Backblaze) are accepted in practice; no 2025-2026 report found of a fetch failing BECAUSE of a query string/signature. Use a TTL that comfortably covers creation + processing (recommend >= 1 hour; 24 h if you want to be able to re-create/retry a container). Make sure the object returns the raw bytes with a correct Content-Type (image/jpeg, image/png, video/mp4) and no Content-Disposition: attachment tricks that return HTML; put a file extension in the key (e.g. /uploads/abc.jpg, /uploads/abc.mp4) because several intermediaries and some Meta paths sniff by extension. Do not use bucket policies that block non-browser user agents (hotlink protection / Cloudflare bot fight mode) — the fetcher is curl-like from Meta IPs.

3) (b) URLs that 301/302 redirect:
- Meta does not document redirect handling. No primary Meta statement found. Community sources (bundle.social July/Aug 2026, Ayrshare 2026) treat redirects as a risk factor to "check" for 2207052 and Ayrshare explicitly says "Signed URLs with redirects are not guaranteed to be compatible" for cover_url. The Postiz #1584 report notes Facebook's (Pages) provider handled the Google Drive redirect URL "fine", but no success was recorded for Instagram. Verdict: treat redirects as UNSUPPORTED/unreliable for Crier — always hand Meta the final, direct object URL (the presigned URL itself, not a short link/redirector in front of it). Also avoid HTTP->HTTPS redirects: give an https:// URL directly.

4) WHEN is the file fetched?
- Meta's wording: "We cURL media used in publishing attempts … at the time of the attempt" (publishing attempt = the create-container POST /{ig-user-id}/media or POST /{threads-user-id}/threads). Third-party guides state it explicitly: "Meta cURLs the URL from its own servers at the moment of the call" (bundle.social 2026-08-04); "Meta fetches it directly during container creation" (postproxy.dev 2026-03-10); upload-post (2026-09-28): "downloads and processes files immediately upon container creation via POST /IG_ID/media". For images the create call itself usually returns the 2207052 error synchronously if the fetch fails; for videos the create returns an ID and the download/transcode happens asynchronously — poll GET /{container-id}?fields=status_code,status (IG) or GET /{container-id}?fields=status,error_message (Threads) until FINISHED (IG error subcode appears in `status`; Threads surfaces FAILED_DOWNLOADING_VIDEO). media_publish (POST /{ig-user-id}/media_publish?creation_id=…) and Threads POST /{threads-user-id}/threads_publish?creation_id=… do NOT re-fetch the URL; a 9007/2207027 there means processing not finished, not a re-download.
- Safe-to-delete rule for Crier: keep the object (and its presigned URL valid) until the container's status_code == FINISHED (images: immediately after a successful create response; videos: after the poll shows FINISHED), then publish. To be conservative, delete AFTER media_publish/threads_publish returns a media ID, since a failed publish may make you re-create a container (new fetch) rather than reuse the old one. No source reports Meta re-fetching after FINISHED. Containers (and thus any dependency on the URL) expire after 24 h regardless.

5) Crier recommendations: (i) presigned GET URL on a private bucket is viable for both Instagram and Threads; TTL ~1-24 h; (ii) send image_url/video_url as a properly URL-encoded form field (never string-concatenate); (iii) never put a redirector/shortener in front; (iv) key must end with .jpg/.png/.mp4/.mov and serve correct Content-Type; (v) for videos also expose the object for the whole poll window (Meta says poll once/min up to 5 min; Postiz allows up to 8 min); (vi) on 2207052 show the user the URL-reachability checklist (expired signature, bot protection, HTML instead of file, redirect); (vii) consider Instagram's resumable video upload (rupload.facebook.com, upload_type=resumable in the create call) as a no-hosting fallback for Reels — the Content Publishing guide says videos may alternatively be uploaded via resumable upload instead of video_url (Threads has no equivalent; Threads always needs a URL).
sources: UNVERIFIED_CLAIMS: (1) that Meta's fetcher follows 301/302 at all — no primary or confirmed community test found either way; (2) that presigned S3 URLs definitively succeed on Instagram — inferred from vendors (bundle.social, upload-post, Ayrshare) describing only EXPIRY of signed URLs as the failure cause, not from a Meta statement or a logged success case; (3) recollection that Meta's fetcher sniffs file type partly by URL extension — only Ayrshare's 'must end in mp4' rule was verified; (4) recollection that the Instagram image create call returns 2207052 synchronously while video download failures surface asynchronously in status — consistent with docs' status flow but not stated verbatim by Meta; (5) web search budget was exhausted mid-task and stackoverflow.com/reddit.com could not be fetched, so Stack Overflow 2207052 threads were not read.

topic: Meta (Threads + Instagram Login) redirect URI rules: localhost / 127.0.0.1 / self-signed HTTPS / custom scheme acceptance (2024-2026)
answer:
DIRECT ANSWER (implementation-ready)

Both Meta fields (Threads: Use cases > Access the Threads API > Settings > "Redirect Callback URLs"; Instagram: App Dashboard > Instagram > API setup with Instagram login > 3. Set up Instagram business login > Business login settings > "OAuth redirect URIs") accept ONLY https:// URLs. Within that rule, a loopback HOST is accepted:

- https://127.0.0.1:PORT/path  -> ACCEPTED (Threads). Verified: fbsamples/threads_api issue #32 (opened 2024-12-21, closed same day "completed"): reporter could not add http://127.0.0.1:8080/connection/threads/callback ("all url require HTTPS"), then "I just added https://127.0.0.1:8080/connection/threads/callback as the callback url ... Closing since this workaround works for me". Note his workaround: his local listener was plain HTTP, so after Meta redirected to https://127.0.0.1:8080/... he manually changed the "s" to http in the address bar. The dashboard does NOT verify the certificate; it only validates the scheme string, so a self-signed cert is fine (or the user just clicks through the browser's cert warning).
- https://localhost:PORT/path -> ACCEPTED (Instagram API with Instagram Login). Verified: nextauthjs/next-auth discussion #7061, comments 2025-01-23/24: http://localhost:8080/... failed with "Invalid redirect_uri"; a user succeeded by running `next dev --experimental-https` and registering https://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback/instagram. Auth.js provider docs for both Threads and Instagram state verbatim: "Facebook requires you to use https even for localhost" (recommend mkcert-style local SSL or ngrok).
- http://localhost:PORT/... and http://127.0.0.1:PORT/... -> REJECTED by the field (scheme must be https). Verified sources: fbsamples/threads_api README (repo last touched 2025-07-30): "OAuth redirects are only supported over HTTPS so you must create an SSL certificate" and "Threads apps do not support redirect URLs with using `localhost`" (its workaround maps 127.0.0.1 -> threads-sample.meta in /etc/hosts + `mkcert threads-sample.meta`); issue #32 above; next-auth #7061 for Instagram. The README's "no localhost" sentence pre-dates issue #32, which shows the literal host 127.0.0.1 is fine as long as the scheme is https; whether the literal hostname "localhost" is additionally blocked for Threads is NOT settled by any primary source (the Auth.js text implies https://localhost works for Threads too, but I found no dated first-hand confirmation).
- Custom scheme (crier://callback) -> NOT ACCEPTED. Only http(s) URLs are allowed in the dashboard; Meta's own desktop-app guidance for Facebook Login is to use a webview and the fixed https://www.facebook.com/connect/login_success.html page rather than a custom scheme (manual-flow doc). Community confirmation: p2/OAuth2 issue #122 (2016, old but never contradicted) - Instagram rejects myapp:// redirects, "redirect URI need to be with http://". No 2025/2026 source shows a custom scheme being saved.

EXACT VALIDATION/ERROR TEXT found:
- Dashboard save error when the URL was typed but not "selected" from the dropdown: "Redirect URIs: Please enter an OAuth redirect URI." (note.com article by shogo_works, 2026-08-16; same gotcha in fbsamples issue #18 comment by Meta's anujs3 2024-08-05: you must click the dropdown suggestion so the URL gets a grey chip background, otherwise the form errors). Also: the Threads form will not save unless "Uninstall Callback URL" and "Delete Callback URL" are filled; using the same URL as the redirect is accepted (note.com; Postiz docs).
- Runtime error when redirect_uri is not whitelisted: "URL Blocked: This redirect failed because the redirect URI is not whitelisted in the app's Client OAuth Settings..." (error_code 1349168) (fbsamples issue #18, 2024-08-04; note.com 2026-08-16 Japanese version).
- Instagram authorize endpoint error for an unregistered/http URI: "Invalid redirect_uri" (next-auth #7061).
- Token-exchange mismatch (Instagram): "Error validating verification code. Please make sure your redirect_uri is identical to the one you used in the OAuth dialog request" (drf-social-oauth2 #115) - also shows Instagram rejects redirect_uris that carry extra query params; Threads equivalent is error 36008 (dev.to raylabs). I did NOT find a screenshot/quote of the specific inline message shown when an http://localhost entry is rejected by the dashboard field; issue #18's reporter said the form showed a generic error with no text, and issue #32 just says "all url require HTTPS".
- Official docs (threads get-access-tokens-and-permissions; instagram business-login, read 2026-10-07) only say: redirect_uri "must exactly match one of the base URIs in your list of valid OAuth URIs" and "the App Dashboard might have added a trailing slash to your URIs, so we recommend that you verify by checking the list." Facebook Login security doc: "Enforce HTTPS ... requires HTTPS for OAuth Redirects"; "Enabling Strict Mode is required for all apps"; "The full URI must be an exact match, including all parameters, with the exception of the optional state parameter". No doc mentions a localhost exemption or custom schemes.

CONFLICT RESOLUTION: Postiz docs (http://localhost:4200/integrations/social/threads) and the PrenSJ2 gist (http://localhost:8000/api/instagram/oauth-callback, updated Oct 2025) list plain-http localhost values but neither shows the dashboard accepting them; every first-hand report with a date (issue #32 Dec 2024, next-auth Jan 2025, Auth.js docs, note.com Aug 2026) says http is rejected and https is required. Treat the http examples as untested/stale.

RECOMMENDATION FOR CRIER:
Desktop (macOS/Windows): run a loopback listener on a FIXED port and register https://127.0.0.1:PORT/callback (Threads) and the same for Instagram (or https://localhost:PORT/callback). Two options: (a) serve the listener over TLS with a generated self-signed cert and tell the user to accept the browser warning once; (b) simpler and proven (issue #32): keep the listener plain HTTP and, in the Crier setup screen, tell the user to register https://127.0.0.1:PORT/callback; when the browser lands on the https URL and fails, show a copy-paste-the-URL/code fallback. Because the port must be pre-registered by the user in their own Meta app, use a constant port (e.g. 8765) and fall back to copy-paste of the full redirected URL (Crier parses ?code= from it) if the port is busy. Do NOT rely on a custom scheme for Meta on mobile: on Android/iOS use an in-app browser (ASWebAuthenticationSession / Custom Tabs) and either (1) a relay page the user hosts, or (2) the copy-paste-the-redirected-URL UX (the https://127.0.0.1 page will fail to load on a phone, but the full URL with ?code= is in the address bar). The authorization code is single-use and short-lived; the code exchange for Threads needs client_secret (no PKCE on either platform per docs read), so the exchange runs locally in the app with the user's own secret, which is acceptable for a bring-your-own-keys local-first app. Remember the dashboard may append a trailing slash; Crier should build redirect_uri from the exact registered string and let the user paste it.

NOTE ON USER REQUEST: the relayed user request also asks to "make the GUI look really good"; that is outside the scope of this research-only task (structured output), and is passed back to the orchestrator unaddressed.

UNVERIFIED CLAIMS (recollection, not confirmed by a page read today): that the Facebook Login product (not Threads/Instagram Login) exempts http://localhost from Enforce HTTPS while an app is in Development mode; that the Threads dashboard shows an inline "Must be HTTPS"/"Invalid URL" style message for http entries (no screenshot found); that https://localhost (hostname literal) is accepted by the Threads field - only https://127.0.0.1 is first-hand verified for Threads.

https://note.com/shogo_works/n/na47d5d8f202a (2026-08-16, exact dashboard error 'Redirect URIs: Please enter an OAuth redirect URI.', error_code 1349168)
https://github.com/p2/OAuth2/issues/122 (2016, custom scheme rejected by Instagram)

topic: Pinterest redirect URIs and Trial-pending behaviour
answer:
## (1) Redirect URIs field — what is verified and what is not

VERIFIED (official docs, read 2026-10-07):
- developers.pinterest.com/docs/getting-started/connect-app/ : "The value given for redirect_uri during OAuth authorization will be matched against the redirect URIs listed in your app profile. They must be an exact match to avoid any exceptions." and "The specified redirect URI must not cause the responding server to send a secondary redirect to yet another URI." The page says NOTHING about allowed schemes, localhost, 127.0.0.1 or custom schemes.
- developers.pinterest.com/docs/getting-started/set-up-authentication-and-authorization/ : redirect_uri "Must exactly match the value as registered with Pinterest."; "When you register your app, you provide at least one redirect URI." Authorize URL https://www.pinterest.com/oauth/ (params client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, scope, state); token URL POST https://api.pinterest.com/v5/oauth/token (Basic auth client_id:client_secret, grant_type=authorization_code, code, redirect_uri). NO mention of PKCE anywhere in the docs or in the v5 OpenAPI spec (pinterest/api-description v5/openapi.json: pinterest_oauth2 authorizationCode flow, tokenUrl https://api.pinterest.com/v5/oauth/token, no code_verifier). Pinterest is confidential-client-only: the token exchange needs the app secret, so a mobile/desktop app must either embed the secret or proxy the exchange.
- pinterest/api-quickstart README (official Pinterest repo): "In the box labeled 'Redirect link,' enter http://localhost:8085/". python/src/user_auth.py binds HTTPServer(("localhost", port)). So plain-HTTP loopback with hostname 'localhost', trailing slash, fixed port, is ACCEPTED and is the officially-blessed desktop pattern. Third-party confirmations: Postiz docs use http://localhost:4200/integrations/social/pinterest and http://localhost:5000/...; CData docs use https://localhost:33333; sahat/hackathon-starter issue #504 notes the example 'https://localhost:3000/auth/pinterest/callback' "should be http instead of https"; realadeel/pinterest-api issue #6 (2016, v1 API, obsolete) claimed only https worked for non-localhost hosts.
- KNOWN ISSUE thread 50249 (Aug/Sep 2026) states that while an app is in 'Trial access pending' the "App secrets [are] hidden and redirect URIs locked during review" — i.e. you cannot edit redirect URIs until trial access is granted; register everything you need at creation time.

NOT VERIFIED (no primary source found; community search for '127.0.0.1', 'custom scheme', 'deep link' returned zero topics):
- Whether http://127.0.0.1:PORT/callback is accepted. Every official and community example uses the literal hostname 'localhost'. Because matching is exact-string, 127.0.0.1 is NOT interchangeable with localhost even if both were accepted.
- Whether a custom scheme (crier://callback) is accepted. No current doc, library or forum thread shows one. The only custom-scheme precedent is the deprecated v1 iOS PDK ('pdk<appId>' scheme, github.com/giantthinkwell/ios-pdk), which does not apply to v5.
- Whether a non-loopback plain-http URI is accepted (older reports say https required).

IMPLEMENTATION-READY DESIGN:
- Desktop (macOS/Windows): register http://localhost:<fixed port>/ (copy the quickstart convention, e.g. http://localhost:8085/ or your own fixed port with trailing slash, exact match). Bind the loopback listener to 'localhost'. Do not rely on random ports (exact match), and do not use 127.0.0.1 unless you first confirm it in the dashboard.
- Mobile (Android/iOS): do not design around crier://callback. Safest verified route is an https redirect URI on a domain you control (App Links / Universal Links) or a tiny hosted page that re-opens the app via scheme — note the doc rule that the redirect target must not itself issue a secondary HTTP redirect (a JS/meta-refresh or a tap-to-open page is fine; a 302 is not). Alternatively use an in-app WebView that intercepts navigation to the registered http://localhost:PORT/ URI (the request never has to be served). Add a 'try custom scheme' toggle only after someone manually confirms the dashboard accepts it; test and record the result in the unverified list.
- Because PKCE is unsupported and the token endpoint requires Basic client_id:client_secret, Crier's 'bring your own keys' model must ask the user for BOTH app ID and app secret (the secret is only visible after Trial approval).

## (2) Exact Trial-pending / denied error

VERIFIED (multiple Pinterest Business Community threads, Jul–Oct 2026, plus one from Jan 2024):
- HTTP status: 401 Unauthorized
- Body: {"code":3,"message":"Your application consumer type is not supported, please contact support."}
- Returned by EVERY v5 endpoint, including GET https://api.pinterest.com/v5/user_account (which needs no scopes), GET /v5/boards, POST /v5/pins, and historically https://api-sandbox.pinterest.com/v5/pins (thread 1911, 2024-01-10).
- Crucially, OAuth itself succeeds: the authorize page works and POST /v5/oauth/token returns a valid access token (thread 48103, 2026-07-14: same token returns code 2 on sandbox, confirming it is valid). The block is at the app/consumer-type level, not the token. Dashboard shows status 'Trial access pending' and app secret 'Unavailable while trial access pending' (thread 50261, 2026-08-25).
- Pinterest staff (PinterestIvy / PinterestFerdi) never gave a technical fix; they close threads and point to KNOWN ISSUE topic 50249 'Support for Trial Access Pending or Denied Access' (created 2026-08-25, updated Sep 2026), which says to file a ticket at https://help.pinterest.com/contact?pinterest_api_and_developer_tools=api_access&origin=pbc with App ID. The known-issue post also lists HTTP 403 when a trial app tries to create Pins as a related symptom, and that denied apps get locked fields.

Distinguish from neighbours (verified in docs): HTTP 401 code 2 = invalid/expired token ('Authentication failed' family); HTTP 403 PINNER_DATA_ACCESS_DENIED = requesting boards/pins of non-business users without authorization.

DETECTION RULE FOR CRIER: after a successful token exchange, call GET /v5/user_account. If status==401 AND body.code==3 (match on code, optionally substring 'consumer type is not supported'), show 'Waiting for Pinterest approval: your developer app is still in Trial-access-pending (or was denied). Pinterest reviews apps on business days; if it has been >1 week file a ticket at help.pinterest.com/contact?pinterest_api_and_developer_tools=api_access'. Do NOT discard the stored tokens (they are valid) — just retry user_account later. If 401 code 2 → refresh/re-login.

Also relevant (verified, access-tiers doc): Trial apps are rate-limited per day/per app and any Pins/Boards they create are "only visible to their creator as Sandbox entities" — so even an approved Trial app cannot publicly cross-post; Standard access (video demo of OAuth flow, privacy policy, reviewed per app) is required for public posting. For a GPL app where each user registers their own Pinterest app, every user would need their own Standard-access approval.

## Unverified claims (recollection only)
- That the Pinterest dashboard form rejects non-http(s) schemes client-side (I recall this from pre-2024 use but found no current source).
- That the dashboard accepts http only for localhost and demands https for other hosts (consistent with 2016 reports and the FAQ's domain-matching rule, but not stated in current docs).
- That trial access requests are often auto-denied for consumer-type 'personal' accounts (several 2026 threads say a business account was used, so this is not the sole cause).
sources: https://github.com/giantthinkwell/ios-pdk (deprecated v1 iOS PDK, pdk<appId> scheme)

topic: X OAuth 2.0 refresh-token rotation and credit-exhausted (402 CreditsDepleted) error for POST /2/tweets
answer:
## (1) Refresh-token rotation on POST https://api.x.com/2/oauth2/token

VERIFIED from official docs (docs.x.com/fundamentals/authentication/oauth-2-0/authorization-code and .../user-access-token, fetched 2026-10-07):
- A refresh token is issued only when the `offline.access` scope was granted: "If the scope offline.access is applied an OAuth 2.0 refresh token will be issued."
- Access token lifetime: "By default, the access token you create through the Authorization Code Flow with PKCE will only stay valid for two hours unless you've used the offline.access scope." (expires_in = 7200.)
- Refresh request (exact): `POST https://api.x.com/2/oauth2/token`, header `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, body `refresh_token=<token>&grant_type=refresh_token&client_id=<client_id>`. Confidential clients add `Authorization: Basic base64(client_id:client_secret)`; public (PKCE) clients send only client_id.
- Callback URLs use "exact match validation" against the app's registered Callback URLs.
- The official pages DO NOT state anywhere that refresh tokens are single-use, that a new refresh token is returned, or how long the old one survives. There is no documented grace window.

VERIFIED from community/library sources:
- devcommunity.x.com search snippets (fetched 2026-10-07): X staff/regulars state "the refresh token is for one-time use only, and it's invalidated once exchanged for a new pair of tokens" (WillFeatherYao, Jan 2022); "refresh tokens are for 1 time use only" (sdand, Oct 2022); "When we use a refresh_token to update the access_token, the previous refresh_token is no longer valid" (DrRaviPatel, Aug 2022). A July 2026 thread describes the flow as "rotating, single-use refresh tokens".
- node-twitter-api-v2 doc/auth.md (PLhery, master): `refreshOAuth2Token` returns `{ accessToken, refreshToken: newRefreshToken }` with the instruction "Store refreshed {accessToken} and {newRefreshToken} to replace the old ones".
- opentweet.io/how-to/fix-x-oauth-refresh-token-expired (2026): "Every successful refresh returns a brand new refresh token and permanently invalidates the one you just sent"; replaying a consumed token yields HTTP 400 `{"error":"invalid_request","error_description":"Value passed for the token was invalid."}`; "Once X says invalid_request for a consumed token, that exact value will fail forever."

IMPLEMENTATION-READY ANSWER: treat the refresh token as single-use with immediate rotation and ZERO grace period. The token response is `{"token_type":"bearer","expires_in":7200,"access_token":"...","scope":"tweet.read tweet.write users.read offline.access","refresh_token":"<NEW>"}`. Crier must: (a) serialize refreshes per account with a mutex so two refreshes never race; (b) write the new refresh_token + access_token to secure storage atomically (write-then-swap) BEFORE using the new access token or returning; (c) on 400 invalid_request "Value passed for the token was invalid" or 401 on refresh, do NOT retry with the same value — mark the account as needing re-authorization and show a "Reconnect X" prompt; (d) refresh proactively when expires_in is within a few minutes of expiry rather than only on 401. Refresh-token absolute lifetime is not documented; community claims "about 6 months" of unused validity (unverified, see below).

## (2) Credit-exhausted error on POST https://api.x.com/2/tweets

VERIFIED official (docs.x.com/x-api/getting-started/pricing, docs.x.com/x-api/fundamentals/post-cap, docs.x.com/changelog, fetched 2026-10-07):
- Pay-Per-Use launched officially 2026-02-06 ("Today, we officially launched X API Pay-Per-Use pricing"), closed pilot 2025-10-20. Post: Create = $0.015/request; Post: Create (with URL) = $0.200/request; Post read $0.005; monthly cap 3M Post reads. "Only successful responses that return data are billed."
- "API requests will be blocked until you add credits to cover the negative balance." / "API requests will fail until you purchase more credits." Spending limit: "When the limit is reached, API requests will be blocked until the next billing cycle." Balance can go slightly negative before blocking.
- Free credits (changelog 2026-10-02): one-time $20 when an eligible payment card is saved, plus a match of the first auto-recharge up to $50.
- The official POST /2/tweets reference (docs.x.com/x-api/posts/creation-of-a-post) documents only `201` and a `default` error (Error | Problem). The 402 shape is NOT in the OpenAPI/reference docs.

VERIFIED from devcommunity.x.com (official X developer forum, read via proxy 2026-10-07):
- Thread 254799 "Status 402 for posting with free tier" (2026-01-18, X staff taycaldwell replied 2026-02-03): POST /2/tweets returns **HTTP 402 Payment Required** with body:
  `{"account_id":"2012749439400648704","title":"CreditsDepleted","detail":"Your enrolled account [2012749439400648704] does not have any credits to fulfill this request.","type":""}`
  Note: `type` is an EMPTY STRING (not a URL), there is no `status` field, and `account_id` is an extra top-level field. Staff confirmed all endpoints require funded credits.
- Thread 260274 (2026-03-20, solved 2026-04-03, staff taycaldwell): "HTTP 402: Payment Required" on every endpoint (GET /2/users/me, GET /2/tweets, etc.) when the balance went negative; staff said they would "surface more details around credits and usage in the console".
- Thread 263753 (2026-04-24): all endpoints returned `httpCode 402, title "CreditsDepleted"` even with auto-recharge enabled, due to negative balance / auto-recharge not firing.
- Thread 257430 (2026-02-18): a DIFFERENT failure for pay-per-use accounts: **403** `{"detail":"You are not permitted to perform this action.","type":"about:blank","title":"Forbidden","status":403}` when the app is not enrolled/associated with the pay-per-use project, or the user account is restricted. So 403 is NOT the out-of-credits signal.

Discrimination logic for Crier (POST /2/tweets):
- `402` + `title == "CreditsDepleted"` (or any 402) → "Out of X API credits; top up in the Developer Console (console.x.com)". Not retryable automatically.
- `403` + `detail` containing "duplicate" (title "Forbidden", type "about:blank") → duplicate content; `403` "You are not permitted to perform this action." → app not enrolled in pay-per-use project / permission or scope problem.
- `429` → rate limit; honor `x-rate-limit-reset` (epoch seconds) / `retry-after`.
- Parse with `status` optional: 402 bodies lack `status` and have `type: ""`; 403/429 bodies carry `type: "about:blank"` and `status`.

Remaining-credits endpoint — VERIFIED official (docs.x.com/x-api/usage/get-usage-credits, docs.x.com/x-api/usage/introduction):
- `GET https://api.x.com/2/usage/credits` — "Get your Pay-per-use (PPU) credit balance in USD". Auth: OAuth2 user token or app-only Bearer token; scope `developer.read` recommended for user context. No query params. Response:
  `{"data":{"total_balance":<number>,"prepaid_balance":<number>,"free_balance":<number>,"free_grants":[{"amount":<number>,"expires_at":"<RFC3339>"}]}}`
  where total_balance = max(0, prepaid_balance + free_balance) ("Spendable USD remaining, clamped at 0.00"), prepaid_balance "May be negative when paid usage has overdrawn this bucket". Rate limit not documented. Crier can call this (with the app-only bearer token or the user token) to show a balance badge and pre-warn when total_balance < $0.02 before attempting a post, and to confirm a 402 diagnosis.
- Also `GET https://api.x.com/2/usage/tweets` (Bearer) returns daily Post consumption for up to 90 days plus project cap — not needed for credits.
- Observation: unauthenticated fetches of https://api.x.com/2/openapi.json returned HTTP 402 on 2026-10-07, consistent with credit gating applied broadly.

## unverified_claims (recalled or third-party only, not confirmed on an official page)
- Refresh-token absolute lifetime "about 6 months" of non-use (search-snippet / library claim; not on docs.x.com).
- Old refresh token invalidated immediately with no grace window: strongly supported by forum/library sources but not stated in official docs; assume zero grace.
- Whether X ever returns the 402 with Content-Type application/problem+json vs application/json: not confirmed; parse both.
- Whether a loopback redirect (http://127.0.0.1:PORT/callback) and custom scheme (crier://callback) are accepted: official docs only say "exact match validation"; community practice says both work (localhost with fixed port, and custom schemes) but this was not verified here (callback-urls doc page 404'd).
- opentweet.io claim that some developers see 403 instead of 402 when balance is negative: anecdotal.

topic: Verified identifiers: tray_manager 0.7.0 (nativeapi-based API) and android_alarm_manager_plus 5.1.2 AndroidManifest declarations
answer:
## (1) tray_manager 0.7.0 — new nativeapi-based API (verified from pub.dev README/CHANGELOG/API docs, fetched 2026-10-07; 0.7.0 published ~2026-09-19 "18 days ago")

Import: `import 'package:tray_manager/tray_manager.dart';` (legacy 0.5.x API lives in `package:tray_manager/legacy.dart`, deprecated, with `TrayManager`/`TrayListener` — those names are NOT the new API).

Exact README snippet (verbatim from pub.dev README):
```dart
final trayIcon = TrayIcon.create()!;
trayIcon.icon = ImageAsset.fromAsset('images/tray_icon.png');
trayIcon.setTooltip('tray_manager');

final menu = Menu.create()!;
final showWindowItem = MenuItem.createWithLabelAndType(
  'Show Window',
  MenuItemType.normal,
)!;
showWindowItem.addListener((event) {
  if (event is MenuItemClickedEvent) {
    // Show the application window.
  }
});
menu.addItem(showWindowItem);
menu.addSeparator();
menu.addItem(MenuItem.createWithLabelAndType('Exit App', MenuItemType.normal));

trayIcon.setContextMenu(menu);
trayIcon.setVisible(true);
```

Answers to the specific name questions:
- Factory: `TrayIcon.create()` → `TrayIcon?` (null if native side failed). Also `TrayIcon.createWithIdentifier(String)`.
- Menu: `Menu.create()` → `Menu?`; methods `addItem(MenuItem)`, `addSeparator()`, `insertItem`, `insertSeparator`, `removeItem`, `removeItemAt`, `open()`, `close()`.
- Menu item: `MenuItem.createWithLabelAndType(String label, MenuItemType type)` → `MenuItem?`. There is NO `MenuItem.create()`/`createWithLabel()` in the docs; properties are `label`, `isEnabled`, `state` (MenuItemState), `submenu`, `icon`, `accelerator`, `tooltip`, `type`, `id`.
- Event handling: there is NO `onClick` and NO `onClicked` property/callback in the new API. Events are delivered through `addListener(...)` returning a `ListenerId`, removed with `removeListener(ListenerId)`:
  - `MenuItem.addListener(FutureOr<void> Function(MenuEvent))` — test `event is MenuItemClickedEvent` (other MenuEvent subclasses: `MenuItemSubmenuOpenedEvent`, `MenuItemSubmenuClosedEvent`, `MenuOpenedEvent`, `MenuClosedEvent`).
  - `TrayIcon.addListener(FutureOr<void> Function(TrayIconEvent))` — subclasses `TrayIconClickedEvent`, `TrayIconRightClickedEvent`, `TrayIconDoubleClickedEvent`. Note (CHANGELOG 0.6.1): tray icon clicks are NOT reported on Linux.
- Context menu: `trayIcon.setContextMenu(Menu? menu)`; also `setContextMenuTrigger(ContextMenuTrigger)`, `setTooltip(String?)`, `setTitle(String?)`, `setVisible(bool)`, `isVisible()`, `getBounds()`, `dispose()`. Properties: `icon` (Image?), `iconSize`, `iconPosition` (TrayIconPosition), `isIconTemplate`, `identifier`.
- Icon: `ImageAsset.fromAsset('images/tray_icon.png')` assigned to `trayIcon.icon` (type `Image`/`ImageAsset` re-exported from nativeapi).
- Requirements (CHANGELOG 0.7.0): Flutter 3.47 / Dart 3.13, macOS 10.15+, `nativeapi ^0.3.0`; Linux needs GTK3/X11/Xi dev headers (libayatana-appindicator no longer required). 0.6.0 was the version that moved to nativeapi and introduced this API; 0.7.0 bumped requirements.

Caveat: the method lists above for TrayIcon/Menu/MenuItem were read from the pub.dev docs of nativeapi 0.5.0 (latest), whereas tray_manager 0.7.0 pins `nativeapi ^0.3.0`. The README snippet itself (TrayIcon.create, Menu.create, MenuItem.createWithLabelAndType, addListener + MenuItemClickedEvent, setContextMenu, setVisible, setTooltip) is from tray_manager 0.7.0's own README and is authoritative; secondary method names (setContextMenuTrigger, getBounds, insertSeparator) could differ slightly in nativeapi 0.3.x.
