unverified_claims (recollection, not confirmed by a fetched page this session): the README also requires `await AndroidAlarmManager.initialize()` before scheduling and `@pragma('vm:entry-point')` on top-level callback functions; on Android 13+ `USE_EXACT_ALARM` can be used instead of `SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM` for alarm-clock/calendar-type apps but Play review scrutinizes it; `exact: true` alarms require the SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM runtime grant on Android 14+ (`canScheduleExactAlarms()`); tray_manager 0.6.0 changelog date ~2026-02 (0.6.x entries were not visible on the fetched CHANGELOG pages).

DIRECT ANSWER: In Misskey 2025.10.0+ scheduling is NOT a parameter on POST /api/notes/create. It is implemented on top of the note-drafts API (introduced 2025.7.0): a draft with isActuallyScheduled=true and a future scheduledAt is a pending scheduled note. The server enqueues a delayed BullMQ job (queue "postScheduledNote", job data {noteDraftId}) and, at fire time, calls NoteCreateService.fetchAndCreate() with the draft's fields and then deletes the draft.

VERIFIED (misskey-dev/misskey develop branch, read 2026-10-07; feature shipped in release 2025.10.0, published 2025-10-08 per GitHub releases page; CHANGELOG line: "Feat: 予約投稿ができるようになりました ... デフォルトで作成可能数は1になっています。適宜ロールのポリシーで設定を行ってください。"):

1) POST /api/notes/create (packages/backend/src/server/api/endpoints/notes/create.ts) — paramDef has NO scheduledAt/schedule property (only visibility, visibleUserIds, cw, localOnly, reactionAcceptance, noExtractMentions, noExtractHashtags, noExtractEmojis, replyId, renoteId, channelId, text, fileIds, mediaIds, poll). No notes/schedule* endpoints exist in endpoint-list.ts; the only related endpoints are notes/drafts/{list,create,delete,update,count}.

2) CREATE a scheduled note: POST /api/notes/drafts/create (requireCredential, permission kind 'write:account', rate limit 300/hour). JSON body (standard Misskey: {"i": token, ...} or Bearer token):
   { "text": "...", "cw": null, "visibility": "public"|"home"|"followers"|"specified", "visibleUserIds": [], "localOnly": false, "reactionAcceptance": null, "replyId": null, "renoteId": null, "channelId": null, "fileIds": ["<misskey:id>", ... max 16], "poll": {choices[≤10], multiple, expiresAt|expiredAfter}, "hashtag": "...", "scheduledAt": <integer>, "isActuallyScheduled": true }
   paramDef verbatim: scheduledAt: { type: 'integer', nullable: true }, isActuallyScheduled: { type: 'boolean', default: false }. The endpoint does scheduledAt: ps.scheduledAt ? new Date(ps.scheduledAt) : null — i.e. scheduledAt is a UNIX EPOCH IN MILLISECONDS (JS Date constructor). You MUST send isActuallyScheduled:true; a draft with scheduledAt alone is just a draft and is never posted. Response: { "createdDraft": NoteDraft }.
   Errors (create.ts): TOO_MANY_SCHEDULED_NOTES id 22ae69eb-09e3-4541-a850-773cfa45e693 ("You cannot create scheduled notes any more."), SCHEDULED_AT_REQUIRED id 15e28a55-e74c-4d65-89b7-8880cdaaa87d, SCHEDULED_AT_MUST_BE_IN_FUTURE id e4bed6c9-017e-4934-aed0-01c22cc60ec1. Service-level validation (NoteDraftService.validate): throws if isActuallyScheduled && scheduledAt==null, or scheduledAt.getTime() < Date.now(). Limits: count of user's drafts with isActuallyScheduled=true must be < role policy scheduledNoteLimit (DEFAULT_POLICIES: scheduledNoteLimit: 1, noteDraftLimit: 10 in RoleService.ts). Also subject to the draft limit.

3) LIST pending scheduled notes: POST /api/notes/drafts/list (kind 'read:account'). Params: limit (1-100, default 30), sinceId, untilId, sinceDate, untilDate, scheduled: boolean|null. scheduled=true → SQL filter drafts.isActuallyScheduled = true (only pending scheduled notes); false → only plain drafts; omitted → all. Returns NoteDraft[]. NoteDraft packed schema fields: id (misskey id), createdAt (ISO date-time string), scheduledAt (type 'number', nullable — epoch ms), isActuallyScheduled (boolean), text, cw, userId, user, replyId, renoteId, visibility, visibleUserIds, fileIds, files, poll, channelId, channel, localOnly, reactionAcceptance, hashtag. POST /api/notes/drafts/count also exists.

4) CANCEL a scheduled note: POST /api/notes/drafts/delete with { "draftId": "<misskey:id>" } (kind 'write:account'; errors NO_SUCH_NOTE_DRAFT 49cd6b9d-848e-41ee-b0b9-adaca711a6b1, ACCESS_DENIED 56f35758-7dd5-468b-8439-5d6fb8ec9b8e). NoteDraftService.delete() removes the row and calls clearSchedule(draftId), which scans postScheduledNoteQueue jobs in states delayed/waiting/active and removes those whose job.data.noteDraftId matches. Alternative "unschedule but keep as draft": POST /api/notes/drafts/update with { "draftId": ..., "isActuallyScheduled": false } (update.ts: scheduledAt integer nullable, isActuallyScheduled boolean, same three scheduling errors; required: ['draftId']). update() always clearSchedule()s then re-schedules if scheduledAt != null && isActuallyScheduled; transitioning false→true re-checks scheduledNoteLimit (error id bacdf856-5c51-4159-b88a-804fa5103be5). RESCHEDULE = drafts/update with a new scheduledAt.

5) Execution: NoteDraftService.schedule() enqueues postScheduledNoteQueue.add(draft.id, {noteDraftId: draft.id}, {delay: scheduledAt - Date.now(), removeOnComplete, removeOnFail}). PostScheduledNoteProcessorService.process() loads the draft (with user); bails if draft/user null, scheduledAt null, or !isActuallyScheduled; then noteCreateService.fetchAndCreate(draft.user, {...}) and removes the draft. Consequence: after it fires, the draft disappears from drafts/list and the note appears in the normal timeline; the API gives no callback — poll notes/drafts/list?scheduled=true and users/notes to detect publication. Accuracy depends on the Redis queue; jobs are delayed, not cron-polled.

6) Forks: CherryPick (kokonect-link/cherrypick develop, package.json version 4.18.0-beta.1, basedMisskeyVersion "2025.12.2") has identical notes/drafts/{count,create,delete,list,update} with the same scheduledAt:{type:'integer',nullable:true} / isActuallyScheduled:{type:'boolean',default:false} and the same three error codes, plus CherryPick-only params (event, disableRightClick, scheduledDelete {deleteAt|deleteAfter}, deliveryTargets). Sharkey: could NOT be verified (activitypub.software returned HTTP 402 to the fetcher; no GitHub/Codeberg mirror found) — see unverified_claims.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES FOR CRIER: use the same access-token flow as normal posting but ensure the token has write:account (not just write:notes) for drafts/create/update/delete and read:account for drafts/list. topic: Bluesky/AT Protocol: granular rpc: OAuth scopes needed for video upload (getServiceAuth + app.bsky.video.*), transition:generic status, and legacy createSession JWT lifetimes
answer:
## (1) rpc: scope strings for video upload under granular permissions

### How the check works (verified from PDS source, bluesky-social/atproto main, read 2026-10-07)
- com.atproto.server.getServiceAuth handler (packages/pds/src/api/com/atproto/server/getServiceAuth.ts): `authorize: (permissions, { params }) => { const { aud, lxm = '*' } = params; permissions.assertRpc({ aud, lxm }) }`. The aud the CLIENT passes is compared as-is against granted rpc: scopes. aud must satisfy `isAtprotoDid(aud) || isAtprotoDidRefAbsolute(aud)` (bare DID or did#serviceId; the did#serviceId form was added in @atproto/pds 0.5.1, PR #4992, merged 2026-05-24). exp max = 1 hour when lxm is set (1 minute if method-less). PROTECTED_METHODS (never issuable) = account/identity methods (updateHandle, createAppPassword, getSession, deactivateAccount, etc.); PRIVILEGED_METHODS = chat.bsky.* + com.atproto.server.createAccount. com.atproto.repo.uploadBlob and app.bsky.video.* are in neither list.
- Scope matching (packages/oauth/oauth-scopes/src/scopes/rpc-permission.ts): `(aud === '*' || aud === options.aud) && (lxm.includes('*') || lxm.includes(options.lxm))` — STRICT string equality on aud, no fragment normalisation. In a scope string, aud must be `*` or an AtprotoDidRefAbsolute (did#serviceId); a bare DID in the scope string is INVALID (test file lists `rpc:foo.bar.baz?aud=did:web` as a null-parse case). `rpc:*?aud=*` (both wildcards) is rejected; `rpc:<lxm>?aud=*` is explicitly valid (test: `rpc:com.example.method1?aud=*` matches `{lxm:'com.example.method1', aud:'did:web:example.com#service_id'}`).
- PDS proxied calls (packages/pds/src/pipethrough.ts, since 0.5.1): scope check uses `scopeAud = did + '#' + serviceId` from the atproto-proxy header (default `did:web:api.bsky.app#bsky_appview`), while the outbound service JWT keeps the bare DID ("Phase 1" comment).

### What the official Bluesky app actually does (verified, bluesky-social/social-app main, read 2026-10-07)
- uploadBlob token: `getServiceAuth({ aud: getServiceAuthAudFromUrl(dispatchUrl), lxm: 'com.atproto.repo.uploadBlob', exp })` where `getServiceAuthAudFromUrl(url)` returns the BARE `did:web:<pds hostname>` (src/lib/strings/url-helpers.ts).
- Limits: `getServiceAuth({ aud: VIDEO_SERVICE_DID, lxm: 'app.bsky.video.getUploadLimits' })` with `VIDEO_SERVICE_DID = 'did:web:video.bsky.app'` (BARE) and `VIDEO_SERVICE = 'https://video.bsky.app'`; the limits call is then made DIRECTLY to https://video.bsky.app/xrpc/app.bsky.video.getUploadLimits with `Authorization: Bearer <service token>` (not proxied through the PDS).
- Upload itself is now MULTIPART, direct to video.bsky.app with the uploadBlob service token as Bearer: /xrpc/app.bsky.video.startUpload (JSON {sizeBytes, mimeType, name?, durationMs?, width?, height?} -> {jobId, partSizeBytes, partCount, expiresAt}), uploadPart, finishUpload, getUploadStatus?jobId=, abortUpload. The legacy single-shot app.bsky.video.uploadVideo (input video/mp4, output {jobStatus}) and getJobStatus still exist in the lexicons. Client constants: VIDEO_MAX_SIZE = 300 MB (300*1000*1000 bytes), VIDEO_MAX_DURATION_MS = 10 min.

### Implementation-ready scope recommendation
Because scope aud is strict-equality and a bare DID cannot appear in a scope string, but the aud you must put in the service JWT is the bare DID (the PDS verifies uploadBlob service JWTs against its own bare DID; the official client uses bare DIDs for both calls), the only granular scopes that match bare-DID getServiceAuth requests are the aud=* forms. Request (space-separated in your client metadata `scope`):

```
atproto
repo:app.bsky.feed.post
blob:video/mp4 blob:image/*           (or blob:*/*)
rpc:com.atproto.repo.uploadBlob?aud=*
rpc:app.bsky.video.getUploadLimits?aud=*
rpc:app.bsky.video.uploadVideo?aud=*
rpc:app.bsky.video.getJobStatus?aud=*
rpc:app.bsky.video.startUpload?aud=*
rpc:app.bsky.video.uploadPart?aud=*
rpc:app.bsky.video.finishUpload?aud=*
rpc:app.bsky.video.abortUpload?aud=*
rpc:app.bsky.video.getUploadStatus?aud=*
```
Compact alternative (one scope, multiple lxm): `rpc?aud=*&lxm=com.atproto.repo.uploadBlob&lxm=app.bsky.video.getUploadLimits&lxm=app.bsky.video.uploadVideo&lxm=app.bsky.video.getJobStatus&lxm=app.bsky.video.startUpload&lxm=app.bsky.video.uploadPart&lxm=app.bsky.video.finishUpload&lxm=app.bsky.video.abortUpload&lxm=app.bsky.video.getUploadStatus` (multi-lxm query form is in the spec; exact multi-value parsing of lxm= repeated params verified only indirectly via the lxm array type — if unsure use the one-scope-per-lxm list).

Alternative via permission set: `include:app.bsky.authCreatePosts?aud=did:web:api.bsky.app%23bsky_appview` (lexicons/app/bsky/authCreatePosts.json: rpc inheritAud:true with lxm = uploadVideo, getJobStatus, getUploadLimits, startUpload, uploadPart, finishUpload, abortUpload, getUploadStatus + repo create app.bsky.feed.post/postgate/threadgate). CAVEAT: with inheritAud the rpc aud becomes `did:web:api.bsky.app#bsky_appview`, which does NOT strictly equal `did:web:video.bsky.app` or the bare PDS DID, and the set contains no `com.atproto.repo.uploadBlob` lxm and no blob permission. So the permission set alone is NOT sufficient for the official-client-style flow; add `rpc:com.atproto.repo.uploadBlob?aud=*`, `blob:*/*` and (for video.bsky.app) the aud=* video scopes, or call getServiceAuth with aud=`did:web:api.bsky.app#bsky_appview`-style did#serviceId (only works if the video service accepts a fragment aud — unverified).

Do NOT request `rpc:*?aud=*` (rejected by the parser). Scope with bare DID (e.g. `rpc:com.atproto.repo.uploadBlob?aud=did:web:video.bsky.app`) is a parse error and silently drops.

### transition:generic on bsky.social, Oct 2026
Still accepted. atproto.com/specs/oauth (read 2026-10-07) lists transition:generic, transition:email, transition:chat.bsky as supported, stating "The goal is to deprecate and eventually remove these transitional scopes" with no timeline. PDS code on main (packages/oauth/oauth-scopes/src/scope-permissions-transition.ts) still implements it: with transition:generic, assertRpc passes for any lxm not starting with `chat.bsky.` (aud ignored), and all blob and repo checks return true. bsky.social runs this PDS distribution (pds 0.5.38 published 2026-10-07). So `atproto transition:generic` remains the zero-risk fallback for video posting today; granular scopes are the forward path.

## (2) Legacy createSession token lifetimes (verified from source, packages/pds/src/account-manager/helpers/auth.ts, read 2026-10-07)
- accessJwt: `createAccessToken(...)` default `expiresIn = '120mins'` -> 2 hours (scope `com.atproto.access`, or `com.atproto.appPass` / `com.atproto.appPassPrivileged` for app-password sessions).
- refreshJwt: `createRefreshToken(...)` default `expiresIn = '90days'` -> 90 days (scope `com.atproto.refresh`, single-use: rotated on com.atproto.server.refreshSession).
- These are hard-coded defaults; there is no PDS env var to change them (packages/pds/src/config/env.ts has none). Read `exp` from the JWT payload rather than hard-coding; schedule refresh at e.g. exp - 5 min for access, and refresh at least every ~80 days (any successful refresh resets the 90-day window) for the refresh token. Note atproto.com/guides/sdk-auth describes these generically as "~1 hour / ~1 week" — that guidance is older than the code; the code values are authoritative for bsky.social.
